messages:
elaine: @marcus quick heads-up — Acme wants a short demo tomorrow at 11:00 PT. Can we temporarily bump their Dedicated pool burst to 8 GPUs for ~30m? Also they asked about any extra cost and whether keys/IP allowlist change is needed.
marcus: short answer: yes we can, but need a few details: which model (large/quant), expected request qps, and region. pricing: burst time is billed pro-rata at the Reserved rate + burst surcharge (~20%).
acme_sre: hi — we'll run rtx-large (fp16), ~40 qps peak, avg seq len ~512, region us-west1. We can keep fallback to hosted if needed. IPs: we'll provide a CIDR for allowlist.
raj: FYI reserving extra GPUs in us-west1 for dedicated pools can take 30–90m if capacity is tight. For a short 30m bump I recommend using the burst policy rather than adding permanent capacity. Burst credits are consumed from their pool; if they don't have credits we can create a temporary burst allowance on the account.
marcus: process steps: 1) confirm pool_id + model variant 2) sales requests temporary burst + duration 3) eng-provisioning flips burst allowance (console or API) 4) we monitor and auto-fallback if latency/KPIs degrade.
elaine: pool_id is pool-acme-08, model rtx-large-v2, variant fp16. Please action — I need confirmation and cost estimate to share with the customer.
marcus: cost rough calc: Reserved rate for rtx-large is $X/hr per GPU (private), burst surcharge ~20%. For 8 GPUs * 0.5h => estimate = 8 * X * 0.5 * 1.2 = ~4.8 * X. I'll follow up with exact numbers after accounting for any committed discounts.
raj: to apply via API (internal ops call) use:
```
POST /internal/v1/dedicated/pools/pool-acme-08/burst 
{ "increase_to_gpus": 8, "duration_minutes": 30, "reason": "Acme demo" }
```
Note: this endpoint is gated by the "ops:bump_burst" permission. If you want console route: Console > Dedicated > pool-acme-08 > Burst policy > "Temporary bump". It shows estimated cost before apply.
acme_sre: thanks — we'll send the CIDR for allowlist now. Also can you confirm keys: do we reuse hosted API key or create a dedicated key scoped to the pool?
marcus: create a scoped API key tied to the pool and env. Easier to rotate after demo. Steps: Console > API Keys > New key > scope: pool-acme-08. Then add the key to allowlist bindings.
elaine: can someone please provision the burst now so I can send confirmation to Acme? Demo is in ~18h but want a dry run today.
raj: I can do a dry run but we need a short maintenance window — applying burst doesn't restart instances but may trigger scheduler moves. I'll schedule a low-impact window in 15m.
deploy-bot: [ops] change requested: pool-acme-08 bump -> 8 GPUs for 30m. Requestor: raj. Status: queued.
marcus: I'll send the cost note to Acme after raj confirms the dry run result.
deploy-bot: [ops] change started: pool-acme-08. ETA: 2m.
deploy-bot: [ops] change complete: pool-acme-08 bumped to 8 GPUs (30m). Metrics: latency P95 within SLO.
elaine: awesome — thanks team. I'll update Acme and ask them to confirm the demo flow.
acme_sre: saw the dry run, perf looks good. Please proceed with the scheduled demo bump tomorrow. Much appreciated!
